_method: primary sources fetched live (AHDB wholesale dairy, ONS PPI, DESNZ quarterly energy prices, Defra egg stats); beef/energy/eggs/food-PPI verified but excluded as immaterial (<~10% y/y). Coffee is from Trading Economics quoting ICE futures — an aggregator, recorded as primary:false. Re-verified 2026-09-02 (fortnightly sweep): butter rolled to the August 2026 AHDB report (−43% y/y, up 4% m/m), arabica to 2 September 2026 (−21.43% y/y).

entries.title: UK wholesale butter down 43% year-on-year
entries.fact: UK wholesale butter averaged £3,450/tonne in the August 2026 reporting period (weeks 31-35, 27 July-30 August 2026), down 43% from £6,050/tonne a year earlier, per AHDB UK wholesale prices; bulk cream was down 41% and mild cheddar down 20% year-on-year in the same report.

quantification.how: AHDB UK wholesale butter price down 43% y/y to £3,450/tonne (from £6,050/tonne) as of the August 2026 reporting period (27 July-30 August 2026)

source.quote: Reporting period: Weeks 31-35 (27 July-30 August 2026). ... Butter | 3,450 | 350 | 3,320 | 4% | 6,050 | −43%

entries.angle: AHDB's August 2026 wholesale report puts butter at £3,450/tonne against £6,050 a year ago — a 43% fall on an input that dominates bakery, brunch and table-service menus. An opener can ask whether that drop is actually showing up in the group's dairy line, site by site.
entries.proof_pairing: COGS/GP% customer results — visibility of whether supplier pricing tracks the wholesale move
entries.caveats: Wholesale price, not contracted supplier price — groups on fixed dairy contracts may not see the fall yet. Butter rose 4% month-on-month (+£130 from £3,320), a second consecutive monthly rise off the low which AHDB attributes to heat-related reductions in UK milk supply, so the short-term direction is up and the y/y gap is narrowing (it was −46% in the July report). Vertical is a coarse proxy — prefer hand-matching to the account's actual menu. UK series (AHDB); do not apply to Ireland accounts. cost_down framing: this is margin relief the account may be leaving with suppliers — open as a visibility question, not a cost scare.

entries.title: Arabica coffee futures down 21% year-on-year
entries.fact: Arabica coffee futures (ICE) stood at 302.69 US cents/lb on 2 September 2026, 21.43% lower than a year earlier.

quantification.how: ICE arabica coffee futures at 302.69 USd/lb on 2 Sept 2026, 21.43% lower than a year ago (Trading Economics quoting ICE futures); GBP impact additionally depends on GBP/USD

source.quote: Coffee fell to 302.69 USd/Lbs on September 2, 2026, down 2.18% from the previous day. ... is down 21.43% compared to the same time last year, according to trading on a contract for difference (CFD)

entries.angle: Arabica futures sit at 303 US cents/lb as of 2 September 2026 — 21% below a year ago, a steeper fall than the 13% gap recorded in August. For a coffee-led group, an opener can reference the easing green-bean market and whether roaster contract prices are following it down.
entries.proof_pairing: COGS/GP% customer results — tracking whether contracted bean prices follow the futures move
entries.caveats: SECONDARY SOURCE (Trading Economics aggregating ICE futures) — the only non-primary entry in the register; replace with a primary series if one becomes fetchable. Live intraday page: the quoted level moves during the trading day (a fetch earlier the same morning read 302.49), and the page's summary panel showed −21.48% against the −21.43% in the body text quoted here. Exchange price in USD, not the roasted/contracted price UK operators pay — GBP/USD and roaster contract lags sit between the two. Futures remain historically elevated despite the y/y fall. Global series, equally relevant to Ireland accounts in principle, but scoped UK-only pending a decision on IE duplication. Vertical is a coarse proxy — prefer hand-matching to the account's actual menu.
